name: Tiyaa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2022. Introduction to Vaghat language. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only known linguistic introduction to any Kwangic language beyond wordlists; likely has a tone section; but describes Vaghat/Kadung [dkg] (vagh1248), the sister language, not Tiyaa — would give cluster-level prosody only.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2021. The Kwaŋ language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (revised version of the 2007 draft).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Revised Kwang (Kadung) paper may fill the empty 'Tones' section of the 2007 draft; sister language, cluster-level evidence only.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Luther Hon, Julius Dabet, Benard Abraham & Innocent Jonah. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Bijim [jbm] Language of Plateau and Bauchi States, Nigeria, with Mention of the Kadung [dkg] and Tiyaa [tyy] Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-033. Dallas: SIL International. 72 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.3 'Phonetic inventory of Bijim-Kadung-Tiyaa' (pp.13-15) gives consonant and vowel charts, vowel length, labialisation/palatalisation; Appendix E p.43 (PDF p.50): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' 348-item Tiyaa wordlist with impressionistic tone marks. a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2020. Change Request 2020-035 (split of [bij] into Bijim [jbm], Kadung [dkg], Tiyaa [tyy]) and New Code Request form for [tyy] (C. Riepe, L. Hon, Y. Danladi, SIL Nigeria).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; identity, location (Boi), classification (Tarokoid), population 6,000; 'published sources' field blank; only literature is a 2017 Gospel of Luke.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2007. The Kwaŋ [Kwang] language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft ms. (printout 5 Sept 2007), 28 pp. [sister language Kadung/Kwang dkg, not Tiyaa]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology: vowels and consonants only; sec. 3.3 'Tones' is an empty heading; no mention of stress. Describes Kadung, not Tiyaa.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004. Tarok and related languages of East-Central Nigeria: nomenclature and subclassification. Draft ms. (held in sibling dir peee1238)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Covers Tarok, Pe, Yangkam, Sur only; no Ya/Tiyaa data; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Longtau, Selbut R. n.d. Jukunoid and Tarokoid in contact: fading delimitations in reverse? (academia.edu 9129192)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Cited by Decker et al. 2021 as containing Vaghat and Kwang comparative examples; unlikely to treat stress but unseen.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kwanka language' (Vaghat-Ya-Bijim-Legeri) — checked for phonology content and bibliography
sources.note: No phonology; bibliography lists Blench 2021 (Kwang), Blench 2022 'Introduction to Vaghat language' (KWEF, academia.edu 67521000), Blench 2023 (Sur-Myet).

sources.citation: Luke Initiative for Scripture Translation (LIST) / SIL Nigeria. c. 2017. Tiyaa orthography statement or phonology write-up accompanying the Gospel of Luke translation (if any exists; unpublished).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: A Luke Partnership translation normally requires an orthography/phonology statement; would be the only Tiyaa-specific prosodic description. Existence unverified.
